_about.what: Published JSC results for the LUT-DNN family, for the Phase 3 controlled comparison (docs/phase3-plan.md sec 3-4). Citation only - nothing here was resynthesized by us.
_about.warning: JSC IS TWO DIFFERENT DATASETS. Rows are only comparable within the same 'dataset' value. See docs/phase3-ledger.md, 2026-08-10.

fields.dataset: openml = hls4ml_lhc_jets_hlf, OpenML 42468, ~830k instances. cernbox = CERNBox LHC Jets, ~986.8k instances. unknown = not stated by the source and not inferable.
fields.encoder_included: true = the LUT count includes the input encoder. false = core only. n/a = the design takes quantized inputs directly and has no separate encoder stage. unknown = not stated.
fields.confidence: verified = read from the cited paper's own table. reported = taken from a secondary source that quotes it. unverified = we have not yet seen the primary source.

_about.our_dataset: openml - upstream DWN's tutorial uses openml.datasets.get_dataset(42468) and our training notebooks use fetch_openml('hls4ml_lhc_jets_hlf'). Our 166k test set is 20% of ~830k.

cernbox.name: CERNBox LHC Jets Dataset
cernbox.note: NeuraLUT-Assemble: 'For the JSC dataset from CERNBox, we focused on comparisons with other LUT-based approaches, as they are the only prior works utilizing this data source.'

offset_pp.how: Measured WITHIN method, twice, in arXiv:2607.08427 Table V: NeuraLUT-Assemble 76.0 (openml) vs 75.0 (cernbox); FPGN 76.0 (openml) vs 74.9 (cernbox). OpenML is the easier of the two.
offset_pp.why_it_matters: Larger than our 0.15 pp noise floor and larger than most differences our Pareto frontier argues about.
